scope: Theorem 9.2 (Two full-box processors on Euclidean space) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every finite machine and input, and every fixed computable ν > 0, either the move-first recorder of Lemma 5.2 or the six-rule recorder of Lemma 6.1 yields effective smooth forcing on R3 with one compact spatial support, all mixed derivatives bounded, and period one for t ≥ 1, such that ∃t ≥ 0 : (Φt(0))1 < −1 ⇐⇒ halting. The zero-data solution is unique in Lemma 7.3’s class, has pressure zero and uniformly bounded energy. Separately, the six-rule processor admits a force square-integrable on all space-time with the same support and event.
